items.title: How much plastic enters the ocean
items.claim: Jambeck et al. (2015, Science) estimated annual plastic input to the oceans from coastal countries. What was the order of magnitude?

options.text: A few hundred tonnes per year
Roughly 4.8-12.7 million tonnes per year (2010 estimate)

items.reveal:
Jambeck et al. (2015) estimated 4.8-12.7 million metric tonnes for 2010. Later estimates (e.g. Borrelle et al., 2020) project rises absent intervention.

The known sinks (surface, beach, deep sea, biota) account for only a fraction of the modelled input, leading to active debate on missing plastic.
items.why: Pollution accounting often produces estimates with wide uncertainty bands but striking headline numbers.

items.title: Solar cost decline
items.claim: Utility-scale solar PV levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) fell by roughly how much between 2010 and 2022?
items.reveal:
IRENA's 2023 cost report found utility-scale solar PV LCOE fell from around $0.45/kWh in 2010 to $0.049/kWh in 2022 in real terms.

Wind and battery costs followed similar trajectories.
items.why: Technology learning curves can outpace policy timelines on energy transition.

items.title: Why the Montreal Protocol worked
items.claim: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out ozone-depleting substances. By the early 2020s what is the projected outcome?

options.text: The ozone layer is on track to recover to 1980 levels around mid-century outside the polar regions
The hole has expanded since the protocol

items.reveal:
WMO/UNEP scientific assessments (2018 and 2022) report stratospheric chlorine peaking in the late 1990s and recovery to 1980 ozone levels by around 2040 outside polar regions; 2066 over Antarctica.

Unreported CFC-11 emissions detected in 2018 were largely addressed by 2021.
items.why: A small group of carefully targeted treaties has produced large measurable atmospheric outcomes.
